help.ABS: Returns the absolute value of a number, that is the number without its sign.

help.MOD: Returns the remainder after dividing two numbers.

help.SIN: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians.
help.SQRT: Returns the positive square root of a number.
help.SUBTOTAL: Returns a subtotal in a list using the function you choose, skipping nested subtotals.
help.SUM: Adds all the numbers in a range of cells.
help.SUMIF: Adds the cells that meet one criterion.
help.SUMIFS: Adds the cells that meet multiple criteria at once.
help.SUMPRODUCT: Multiplies corresponding array elements and returns the sum of the products.
help.SUMSQ: Returns the sum of the squares of the arguments.
help.TAN: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians.
help.TRUNC: Truncates a number to an integer by removing the decimals, without rounding.
help.AVERAGE: Returns the average of its arguments.
help.AVERAGEIF: Returns the average of the cells that meet one criterion.
help.AVERAGEIFS: Returns the average of the cells that meet multiple criteria at once.
help.COUNT: Counts how many cells in a range contain numbers.
help.COUNTA: Counts how many cells in a range are not empty.
help.COUNTBLANK: Counts the empty cells in a range.
help.COUNTIF: Counts the cells that meet one criterion.
help.COUNTIFS: Counts the cells that meet multiple criteria at once.

help.RANK_EQ: Returns the rank of a number in a list - equal numbers get the same rank.

help.STDEV_P: Calculates standard deviation based on the entire population.
help.STDEV_S: Estimates standard deviation based on a sample.
help.VAR_P: Calculates variance based on the entire population.
help.VAR_S: Estimates variance based on a sample.
help.AND: Returns TRUE when all arguments are true.
help.IF: Checks a condition and returns one value if it is true and another if it is false.
help.IFERROR: Returns a value you specify when the formula produces an error, otherwise the formula result.
help.IFNA: Returns a value you specify only when the formula produces #N/A.
help.IFS: Checks successive conditions and returns the value of the first one that is true.
help.NOT: Reverses the logical value of its argument.
help.OR: Returns TRUE when at least one argument is true.
help.SWITCH: Compares an expression against a list of values and returns the result of the first match.
help.XOR: Returns TRUE when an odd number of the arguments are true.
help.CHOOSE: Picks a value from a list based on an index number.
help.HLOOKUP: Looks up a value in the first row of a table and returns a value from the row you specify.
help.INDEX: Returns the value of a cell inside a range, given a row and column number.
help.LOOKUP: Looks up a value in one row or column and returns the matching value from a second one.
help.MATCH: Returns the position of a value inside a range, not the value itself.
help.VLOOKUP: Looks up a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from the column you specify.
help.CHAR: Returns the character matching a code number.
help.CODE: Returns the numeric code of the first character of a text.
help.CONCAT: Joins text from several ranges or strings into one.
help.EXACT: Checks whether two texts are exactly the same, case sensitive.
help.FIND: Finds the position of one text inside another, case sensitive.
help.LEFT: Returns the first characters of a text.
help.LEN: Returns the number of characters in a text.
help.MID: Returns part of a text, from the position and for the length you specify.
help.PROPER: Capitalises the first letter of each word.
help.REPLACE: Replaces part of a text based on its position.
help.REPT: Repeats a text as many times as you specify.
help.RIGHT: Returns the last characters of a text.
help.SEARCH: Finds the position of one text inside another, case insensitive.
help.SUBSTITUTE: Replaces one text with another, based on content rather than position.
help.T: Returns the argument when it is text, otherwise empty text.
help.TEXTJOIN: Joins texts with a delimiter, optionally ignoring empty ones.
help.TRIM: Removes extra spaces from text, keeping single spaces between words.
help.ERROR_TYPE: Returns the number matching an error value.
help.ISBLANK: Returns TRUE when the cell is empty.
help.ISERR: Returns TRUE for any error except #N/A.
help.ISEVEN: Returns TRUE when the number is even.
help.ISLOGICAL: Returns TRUE when the value is logical.
help.ISNA: Returns TRUE only for the #N/A error.
help.ISNONTEXT: Returns TRUE when the value is not text.
help.ISNUMBER: Returns TRUE when the value is a number.
help.ISODD: Returns TRUE when the number is odd.
help.ISTEXT: Returns TRUE when the value is text.
help.N: Converts a value to a number.
help.NA: Returns the #N/A error, meaning the value is not available.
help.TYPE: Returns a number indicating the type of the value.

SUM.0: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want to add up.
SUM.1: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want to add up.

AVERAGE.0: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the average of.
AVERAGE.1: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the average of.

MIN.0: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the smallest value of.
MIN.1: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the smallest value of.

MAX.0: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the largest value of.
MAX.1: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want the largest value of.

PRODUCT.0: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want to multiply.
PRODUCT.1: number1;number2;… are 1 to 255 numbers, cells or ranges you want to multiply.

COUNT.0: value1;value2;… are 1 to 255 values, cells or ranges. Only entries containing numbers are counted.
COUNT.1: value1;value2;… are 1 to 255 values, cells or ranges. Only entries containing numbers are counted.

COUNTA.0: value1;value2;… are 1 to 255 values, cells or ranges. Every entry that is not empty is counted.
COUNTA.1: value1;value2;… are 1 to 255 values, cells or ranges. Every entry that is not empty is counted.

ROUND.0: number is the number you want to round.
ROUND.1: num_digits is the number of decimal places to round to. Zero rounds to the nearest integer; a negative value rounds to the left of the decimal point.

ROUNDUP.0: number is the number you want rounded up, away from zero.
ROUNDUP.1: num_digits is the number of decimal places to round to. Zero rounds to the nearest integer; a negative value rounds to the left of the decimal point.

ROUNDDOWN.0: number is the number you want rounded down, toward zero.
ROUNDDOWN.1: num_digits is the number of decimal places to round to. Zero rounds to the nearest integer; a negative value rounds to the left of the decimal point.

ABS.0: number is the real number you want the absolute value of, that is, without its sign.

INT.0: number is the real number you want rounded down to the nearest integer.

SQRT.0: number is the number you want the square root of. A negative number returns #NUM!.

POWER.0: number is the base, any real number.
POWER.1: power is the exponent the base is raised to.

MOD.0: number is the number you want the remainder of after division.
MOD.1: divisor is the number to divide by. Zero returns #DIV/0!.

CONCATENATE.0: text1;text2;… are 1 to 255 text strings to be joined into a single text string, and can be text strings, numbers, or single-cell references.
CONCATENATE.1: text1;text2;… are 1 to 255 text strings to be joined into a single text string, and can be text strings, numbers, or single-cell references.

LEFT.0: text is the text string containing the characters you want to extract.
LEFT.1: num_chars specifies how many characters are returned from the start. If omitted, one character is returned.

RIGHT.0: text is the text string containing the characters you want to extract.
RIGHT.1: num_chars specifies how many characters are returned from the end. If omitted, one character is returned.

MID.0: text is the text string containing the characters you want to extract.
MID.1: start_num is the position of the first character to extract. The first character of the text is 1.
MID.2: num_chars specifies how many characters are returned from the starting position onward.

LEN.0: text is the text whose length you want. Spaces count as characters.

TRIM.0: text is the text from which to remove extra spaces, except for single spaces between words.

UPPER.0: text is the text you want converted to uppercase.

LOWER.0: text is the text you want converted to lowercase.

IF.0: logical_test is any value or expression that can be evaluated to TRUE or FALSE.
IF.1: value_if_true is the result when the logical test is TRUE. If omitted, TRUE is returned.
IF.2: value_if_false is the result when the logical test is FALSE. If omitted, FALSE is returned.

IFERROR.0: value is any value, expression or reference that is checked for an error.
IFERROR.1: value_if_error is the result when the value evaluates to an error.

AND.0: logical1;logical2;… are 1 to 255 conditions to test. The result is TRUE only if all of them are TRUE.
AND.1: logical1;logical2;… are 1 to 255 conditions to test. The result is TRUE only if all of them are TRUE.

OR.0: logical1;logical2;… are 1 to 255 conditions to test. The result is TRUE if any one of them is TRUE.
OR.1: logical1;logical2;… are 1 to 255 conditions to test. The result is TRUE if any one of them is TRUE.

NOT.0: logical is a value or expression that evaluates to TRUE or FALSE, whose result is reversed.

SUMIF.0: range is the range of cells the criteria are applied to.
SUMIF.1: criteria is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells are added.
SUMIF.2: sum_range are the cells actually added up. If omitted, the range itself is added.

SUMIFS.0: sum_range are the cells to add up.
SUMIFS.1: criteria_range1 is the range the first condition is applied to.
SUMIFS.2: criteria1 is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells of the matching criteria range count.

COUNTIFS.0: criteria_range1 is the range the first condition is applied to.
COUNTIFS.1: criteria1 is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells of the matching criteria range are counted.

AVERAGEIFS.0: average_range are the cells to average.
AVERAGEIFS.1: criteria_range1 is the range the first condition is applied to.
AVERAGEIFS.2: criteria1 is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells of the matching criteria range count.

MAXIFS.0: max_range are the cells the largest value is returned from.
MAXIFS.1: criteria_range1 is the range the first condition is applied to.
MAXIFS.2: criteria1 is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells of the matching criteria range count.

MINIFS.0: min_range are the cells the smallest value is returned from.
MINIFS.1: criteria_range1 is the range the first condition is applied to.
MINIFS.2: criteria1 is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells of the matching criteria range count.

COUNTIF.0: range is the range of cells the criteria are applied to.
COUNTIF.1: criteria is the condition, as a number, expression or text, that defines which cells are counted.

VLOOKUP.0: lookup_value is the value to be found in the first column of the table.
VLOOKUP.1: array is the range to search within. It must have two or more columns — a single-column range returns #N/A.
VLOOKUP.2: col_index_num is the column number in the table from which the value is returned. The first column is 1.
VLOOKUP.3: range_lookup is a logical value: FALSE for an exact match, TRUE or omitted for an approximate match on a sorted first column.
